comments.author: codex
comments.text: Owner answer recorded for original question 2: Board, Schematic, and future editor/model spaces are distinct surfaces that may remain simultaneously visible in a user-configurable pane tree. Split, tile, retarget, resize, maximize, and temporary fullscreen are required for speed; selecting one editor does not replace the whole central surface. Pane composition is workspace/session state, not design authority. Existing evidence: current running Board/Schematic split and docs/gui/prototypes/workspace-panes.html.

comments.author: codex
comments.text: Owner answer recorded for original question 3: Symbol and Footprint authoring remain separate specialist editor surfaces because their contracts are substantial, while entry is deliberately local and contextual for speed. A selected object exposes the relevant editor through its local menu and opens it in a nearby pane with parent context preserved; direct Library entry also remains available. Footprint direction includes source-assisted construction, parametric pad/outline shaping, standards-derived mask/paste features, and driving physical dimensions. Follow-up 3a owns exact split/retarget/return choreography; asset authority remains a separate question.

comments.author: codex
comments.text: Owner follow-up 3a recorded: contextual Symbol/Footprint entry opens a new adjacent pane by default, keeps the invoking editor visible, and places the asset in its specialist editor type. One keystroke closes the transient pane and restores the preceding layout. This is an initial default rather than a permanent restriction on user-configurable placement. Asset authority and save/commit semantics remain separate questions.

Workspace is the umbrella interaction concept; Editable Workspace covers all authoritative non-publication editing, whether spatial canvas or non-spatial editor, while Paper Space is the publishable/composition workspace class. Domains retain their own editor types and contexts. One terminology follow-up remains: retain Model Space as an exact synonym or retire it from canonical vocabulary.

comments.author: codex
comments.text: Owner answers recorded for original question 6 and blank/template follow-up: Publish Space is the working environment and owns a user-extensible collection of Sheets; it is not itself a Sheet. Sheet exclusively means one publishable page with page/media definition, zero or more viewports, and publish-owned content. Continuous schematic Design Space has no sheet/page object. A Sheet may start blank, while a user-selected custom template may prepopulate it without restricting later customization.

Context menu versus double-click and adjacent-versus-retarget pane behavior remain visual/usability decisions, not authority semantics.

title: DWT: notify user KDE 'disable touchpad while typing' blocks Space-drag pan
description: KDE Wayland default 'Disable while typing' suppresses touchpad motion whenever a key (incl. held Space) is down, blocking the Space+left-drag pan gesture. First client of the notification backbone: condition-bound sticky banner. Startup probe parses ~/.config/kcminputrc [Libinput][vid][pid][dev] groups — key DisableWhileTyping is ABSENT at the blocking default (present only once user unchecks it), so absence=trap-live is a deterministic signal. Escalate severity if no external mouse is enumerated (touchpad is the only pan device). Action button launches 'systemsettings kcm_touchpad'. Banner auto-clears when probe sees the fix. GNOME sibling adapter later (gsettings org.gnome.desktop.peripherals.touchpad disable-while-typing).

title: Pin PreservedUnreadable + expected-generation -> RepositoryUnreadable in the gated GP-CM05E suite
description:
GP-CM05E follow-up from audit of a498f54f (refusal-precedence fix). The commit_mutation !writable() guard also covers PreservedUnreadable (not only MigrationRequired): post-fix an expected-generation mutation on a PreservedUnreadable store surfaces the typed RepositoryUnreadable refusal first; pre-fix it masked as StaleGeneration (status.generation()=None). Correctness improvement by-construction, non-blocking, currently UNPINNED.

PIN TO ADD (gated suite tests/preferences_acceptance_support.rs): PreservedUnreadable store + SetUser(expected=Generation(ref)) as human_cli -> error.code == repository_unreadable, store bytes untouched. Falsifiable: revert the precedence reorder -> flips to stale_generation.

A1 INTENDED: yes. Guard is !self.service.status().writable() (writable()=DefaultsOnly|Ready only, service.rs:46-48), deliberately mirroring the lower service_mutation.rs:100 guard so EVERY non-writable status surfaces its refusal_for_status refusal before validate_expectation. PreservedUnreadable -> UnreadableRepository -> PreferenceErrorCodeV1::RepositoryUnreadable (product_model.rs:442, repository_unreadable) is the pre-existing refusal_for_status mapping (service.rs:372-374). Consistent with MigrationRequired; flagged in the finding packet.

A2 SEED ROUTE: the corrupt-store legitimate-damage pattern. Seed one valid journaled generation (write_generation + promote_head, as acceptance_support/portable_upgrade already does) then damage the head bytes (truncated-head) so repository.inspect() returns Unreadable -> PreservedUnreadable. Python harness already drives it: producer.py _seed_corrupt_store(work, truncated-head) (corrupt-store CLI family; describe -> repository_status=preserved_unreadable). Gated Rust pin: write a valid generation, fs-truncate the head file, open the product service via FixedPreferenceLocationProvider, attempt the expected-generation SetUser, assert repository_unreadable + no write. No new product seam.

title: GP write-refusal banners not exposed via AT-SPI -- screen-reader users receive no refusal feedback
description:
OBSERVED (GP-CM05E F2 Phase-0 refusal-reachability probe, frontend-dev-01): the Global Preferences write-refusal banners are rendered as GPU pixels ONLY and are NOT exposed via AT-SPI. A screen-reader user who triggers a write refusal gets NO accessible notification that their write did not land -- a SILENT FAILURE for exactly the section-6 accessibility-transport audience this product treats as first-class.

EVIDENCE: two retained screenshots under .datum/scratch/frontend-dev-01/f2-set-reset-refusal/phase0-probe/ -- competing-889zqj72/competing-final.png shows the red banner 'writer lease is unavailable'; stale2-*/stale-refined-final.png shows 'expected repository head does not match current head'. An AT-SPI tree scan over the open dialog in BOTH runs found NO node carrying the banner text (matched only an unrelated terminal node), confirming the banner is pixel-only -- consistent with the standing finding that AT-SPI does not expose GPU-rendered GP text/extents.

IMPACT: section-6 N06 requires the refusal to be truthfully surfaced to accessibility transport (AT-SPI tree/events + screen-reader spoken output). A pixel-only banner is announced to sighted users but is invisible to a screen reader -> the stale and competing-writer refusals are silent for screen-reader users.

NOTE (capture bar unchanged): this does NOT soften the F2 acceptance predicate -- the recipe correctly observes pixel-banner + objective no-write (generations/ count) REGARDLESS of the eventual accessibility fix; the capture bar does not relax when the product improves. Capture-and-return per frontier discipline; not a fix request.

Corrected runtime probe (ANNOUNCEMENT-EVENT-DETERMINATION.md): the GP write-refusal fires a real Object.Announcement EVENT carrying the exact typed message at assertive priority (detail1=2) AND exposes a persistent Status node (role=status bar, name 'Global Preferences status') whose Description carries the typed message; no-write still objectively holds (generations unchanged). title: Main application window exposes no AT-SPI frame/window node while mapped; no FOCUSED state on main-window content
description:
Main application window exposes no AT-SPI frame/window node while mapped; no FOCUSED state on main-window content.

While the datum-gui main window IS mapped (launch asserts "window visible"), its own-app AT-SPI tree contains only {application, terminal} nodes -- there is NO frame/window node, and no node ever holds the FOCUSED state. Dialogs/modals DO get proper dialog nodes with FOCUSED controls (so the gap is specific to the main application window). A screen-reader user therefore gets no main-window frame/title and no focus signal for the main window's own content; focus-return after a dialog closes is unobservable.

Repro:
1. Launch datum-gui project-free via the owned-Weston StartupQA envelope (wayland/1.0/1024x900); the window is mapped.
2. Dump the own-app AT-SPI tree (Atspi, PID-filtered): roles = {application, terminal} only (2 nodes); NO frame/window node; nothing FOCUSED.
3. Open Global Preferences (Edit > Preferences) -> a proper dialog node appears (11 nodes). Close it -> back to {application, terminal}, still no frame node, still nothing FOCUSED.
4. Repeat with a project loaded (--project-root <seeded>): 19 nodes (buttons/entries/panels populate) but STILL no frame/window node and STILL no FOCUSED node -- at launch or after GP close.

Evidence (frontend session probes): scratchpad/mainwindow_atspi_probe.py + mainwindow_atspi.json (project-free: 2 nodes, no frame, no focus); seeded_focus_preflight.py + seeded_focus.json (seeded: 19 nodes, still no frame/FOCUSED after GP close); gp_state_probe.py + gp_state.json (top nodes = application only; focus-after-close = none).

Distinct from #9 (dat-newproject-refusal-announce-ukcn): that is the announcement channel; this is tree structure / windowing. #9's fix would not close this.

Relation to pin-2 native coverage (paused): this blocks native recipe N01 close-focus-return and N06 focus-return (OWED-with-disclosure) -- they become readable once a main-window frame node + content FOCUSED state exist. The OWED-list citation of this bead is part of the paused pin-2 GP milestone disposition bookkeeping, to be batched with the eventual pin-2 delivery, not now.

One-task workflow record (PM059, 0c4eb49a):
- Grant: PM-Agent-01 standing appointment (3cdeb4ec).
- Implementer: frontend-dev-01.
- File scope: gui-app main-window AT-SPI / windowing paths (nonconflicting). Queues behind frontend-dev-01's active regression unit.
- No per-fix Frontier item/lease/completion graph/qualification campaign (routine fix).

Source: frontend scratch leg2/native-recipe-fixes/BEAD-READY-mainwindow-atspi-frame.md. Ordinary standalone product defect (uev/icbx/typb pattern).

title: New Project Create refusal (source-changed-since-preview) emits no accessibility announcement
description:
New Project Create refusal (source-changed-since-preview) emits no accessibility announcement.

When the global Units source changes between the New Project modal's pinned preview and pressing Create, the engine correctly refuses ("Global Units source changed since preview", project_genesis.rs:99): the modal stays open, the draft is retained, and no project is created. But the refusal fires NO AT-SPI object:announcement (neither polite nor assertive), so a screen-reader user gets no spoken signal that Create was refused or why -- they must infer it from the modal staying open.

Distinct from the mv1k fix (commit f87cbf05), which wired the New Project modal OPEN and use-project-name mode-change into the announce_console/events machinery. The REFUSAL branch was never wired into that same channel: the precedent and mechanism already exist, so this is a missing announce call on the refusal branch, not a new mechanism. Also distinct from the main-window AT-SPI frame-node gap (defect #8): that is tree structure; this is the announcement channel -- #8's fix would not close this.

Repro (from the N04 refusal drive, ordinary surfaces):
1. CLI-seed the global store (preferences set datum.units.system imperial; missing -> gen0).
2. Open the New Project modal (its preview pins the Global source); type a draft name + an isolated Location; confirm Create is ENABLED.
3. While the modal is open, mutate a global pref via ordinary CLI (preferences set datum.units.system metric, --expected the gen0 GenerationRef).
4. Press Create -> engine refuses (project_genesis.rs:99); modal stays open, draft retained, no project created.
5. Observe the a11y announcement channel (Atspi object:announcement): NO announcement fires for the refusal.

Evidence: the N04 refusal capture payload -- refusal.assertive_announcement == false and the captured refusal_announcements contain only folder-browser navigation events, no refusal announcement (frontend scratch leg2 native_N04_fix4.json; reproducible via the staged recipe's drive_n04 refusal phase).

Impact: screen-reader users pressing Create after the Global source changed get no spoken signal that creation was refused or why.

Relation to pin-2 native coverage: the N04 native recipe assertion is behaviorally observable WITHOUT this announcement (no-project + modal-open + draft + focus), so the pin-2 native recipe does NOT depend on this fix -- it is a standalone product-a11y improvement. Surfaced during the PM-ratified N04 global-refusal-draft-focus redesign (GP-CM05E campaign).

Source: frontend scratch leg2/native-recipe-fixes/BEAD-READY-newproject-refusal-silent.md. Captured as an ordinary standalone product defect (uev/icbx/typb pattern), not a GP-CM05 lane edit. Assigned to frontend-dev-01 for the in-tree Rust fix.
close_reason: Fixed by d02a6edb (announce the New Project Create refusal to the accessibility channel). PM059 one-review satisfied: audit-agent-01 binding bytes-recheck on the committed d02a6edb bytes (blob c9bf22d0). Routine one-task fix; closure evidence recorded in-task, no separate receipt commit.

title: responsive-render/narrow must catch GP dialog clipping with a visual predicate
description:
OBSERVED DEFECT (now fixed, by the clamp commit in this delivery): the detached Global Preferences window opened at a fixed 960x720 regardless of the output. At wayland/1.0/720x760 it overflowed the output by ~240px and the value controls were visually inoperable (clipped past the right edge). Evidence: the gp-cm05e-gui-capture-720x760 packet (PM-inspected pixels); the governing prototype docs/gui/prototypes/preferences-window.html (the @media max-width:980px block, ~L262) mandates no sideways scroll / no clipped control in the narrow layout. Fix: clamp the initial Global Preferences window size to the available work area/output, floored at MIN_PREFERENCES_SIZE (700x540), in crates/gui-app/src/windows/global_preferences_window.rs; the governed narrow layout then engages. Verified post-fix at 720x760: prefs window 720x720, narrow layout engaged, 11 controls within the viewport (evidence: gp-clamp-fix-check packet).

REMAINING ACCEPTANCE REQUIREMENT (why this bead stays open): when the responsive-render/narrow/default/gui/(wayland,1.0,(720,760)) case is built, its predicate MUST assert visual non-clipping via PIXEL-geometry (control bounding boxes within the viewport, or golden-style evidence). AT-SPI presence/enumeration passes WHILE clipped (that is how this defect slipped past the clean-install predicate, legitimately out of its scope), and AT-SPI Component extents are UNAVAILABLE for these GPU-rendered controls (verified) -- so extents cannot be used; pixel-geometry is the mandatory predicate shape.

BREAKPOINT RECONCILIATION: the native narrow-layout breakpoint and the governed prototype breakpoint DIFFER. Native: let narrow = window.width < 800.0; (crates/gui-render/src/global_preferences_dialog.rs:105). Prototype: @media (max-width: 980px) (docs/gui/prototypes/preferences-window.html). The 800-980 logical-px band therefore uses the WIDE layout natively while the governed design specifies narrow -- a potential residual-clipping gap the clamp does NOT address (the clamp only guarantees the window fits the output; within 800-980 the wide layout's fixed 340px label + right-aligned control can still overflow). Reconcile through the owning route (ETM route workspace-documentation-and-revision) when building this family.

REFERENCES: clamp fix commit (this delivery); audit-agent-01 BLESS (independent source + pixel review); retained packets .datum/scratch/frontend-dev-01/gp-clamp-fix-check/PACKET.md and .datum/scratch/frontend-dev-01/gp-clipping-investigation/PACKET.md.

title: Terminal Left Arrow inserts U+E006 instead of moving the input cursor
description: Owner report in Datum terminal: six Left Arrow presses inserted six U+E006 characters into the agent prompt, preventing text editing. Scope proposed: first-party terminal-core keyboard encoder and focused protocol regression tests. title: T1b: Build the Datum-owned TerminalCore

DTC-P14: Implement literal search and a bounded Datum-owned non-backtracking regex engine. DTC-P15: Complete keyboard, keypad, kitty keyboard, mouse, focus, paste, IME-commit, reply, and clipping protocols. DTC-P16: Implement bounded metadata and security events for links, clipboard, shell marks, palette, title, CWD, notifications, URI, and paste. DTC-P17: Implement bounded Datum-owned Base64, checksums, Adler-32, zlib/DEFLATE, and PNG decode. DTC-P18: Implement bounded sixel semantics. DTC-P19: Implement bounded full kitty graphics semantics. comments.author: bfadmin
comments.text: DIAGNOSIS (read-only, 2026-08-14). DEFECT A root cause: KeyboardFocus::Terminal is armed by ONE over-broad entry rule — select_hit_target (main.rs:2219) treats every terminal-panel hit target as deliberate entry, and push_activity_hit_region (bottom_dock.rs:612) makes activity rows span nearly the full dock width, so ANY click in the panel mid-band silently hands the keyboard to the PTY. The state is INVISIBLE (Runtime-private field, never published to ReviewWorkspaceState; status-bar 'focus' is pane content — an unrelated axis) and KEYBOARD-INESCAPABLE: the raw-PTY arm (keyboard_focus.rs:142-148) returns true unconditionally and writes Escape as 0x1b to the shell, making the designed release-to-Editor arm dead code. Exits: canvas click or dock close only. Gate logic itself verified correct; single keyboard->PTY path confirmed. DEFECT B root cause: render_terminal_lane (bottom_dock.rs:238-458) has NO screen-vs-summary decision — chrome (title/session/hints/SESSIONS/4 ACTIVITY SPANS rows) is laid top-down and the emulated screen gets leftovers; at default 220px dock max_lines collapses to the .max(1.0) floor with the single row drawn 11px BELOW the content rect, showing lines.last() = the protocol seed string. PTY is told 9 rows via a 76px chrome estimate the renderer overspends by ~100px. ACTIVITY SPANS is a deliberate summary view (terminal_activity_snapshot.rs), NOT the pan-trace sink; screen content IS produced and stored (apply_bytes_with_responses) — pure layout/space-budget defect. Shared-buffer contamination: push_terminal_line injects GUI status text into the VT grid; resize_grid never clears seed lines. ALL FIXES AWAIT OWNER PACKET per standing directive.

title: Project validation reports a busy writer lock as corrupt JSON and incompatible schema
description:
Reproduced during owner-authorized bounded bug hunt using a disposable native project created through datum-eda project new. project validate succeeds before and after a temporary writer lock; while .datum/revision/writer.lock is held by a diagnostic process, validation returns exit 1, valid=false, schema_compatible=false, code=invalid_json, although the actual message is project write refused: live writer or unavailable lock. No design content changed. This can mislead a designer or agent into treating normal concurrent activity as damaged JSON or incompatible schema.
Source: crates/cli/src/commands/project/validate.rs:53-71 maps every ProjectResolver error into invalid_json and finalizes schema_compatible=false without distinguishing busy/unavailable validation. Expected: report transient busy/unavailable status accurately and avoid claiming content/schema invalidity without inspecting it; preserve writer exclusion.
Reproduction: create native project with factory units; validate (exit 0); hold exclusive flock on existing writer.lock and invoke validate (exit 1 / invalid_json); release lock; validate (exit 0). Existing repository source confirms classification defect. Evidence: .datum/scratch/terminal-bughunt-yqkbdlh1/summary.json and validate-before.stdout, validate-busy.stdout, validate-after.stdout. Built release CLI SHA256 c8c2e13074011815a6ccd9c53d8e2147c14dedb02592477e5fa709caa93049fa. Local evidence is untracked/prunable, not claimed committed. No active project or GUI touched, no product fix or PASS claimed.
